body: Star Wars: Rogue Squadron is Factor 5 and LucasArts' arcade flying game about Luke Skywalker leading Rebel pilots against the Empire. Missions take the squadron across planetary surfaces to attack targets, protect allies, rescue civilians and gather information. The player flies familiar Star Wars craft with different weapons and handling. The emphasis stays on understanding an immediate operation rather than managing a complex cockpit. A vehicle or settlement on the ground can become the reason to turn away from a tempting enemy fighter overhead.

Each mission has its own combination of targets and people to defend. Watching the whole situation matters because defeating every visible enemy may leave the important objective exposed. Hidden upgrades improve the available craft, while performance is assessed against medal requirements after the operation. Those goals encourage returning to a known mission with a more efficient route. Familiarity changes the flight from a first attempt at survival into a sequence of deliberate turns, attacks and checks on the allies who still need protection.

The Windows edition appeared a few days before the Nintendo 64 version in December 1998. On Nintendo's console, the optional Expansion Pak enabled a higher display resolution. Factor 5 developed the engine and sound technology while LucasArts contributed the story and mission design. The earlier snowspeeder sequence in Shadows of the Empire helped inspire the focus on planetary flight. Rogue Squadron expanded that idea into a complete campaign, later followed by GameCube sequels that carried the squadron's combination of clear objectives and cinematic aerial action onto another generation.
